small_guidance:
- Add larger-K autotune configs (BLOCK_K=128) and try BLOCK_M=128/BLOCK_N=128 with num_stages=5, num_warps=8 — K=4096 is large and deeper pipelining can hide global load latency better than the current 3-4 stages.
- Cast loads of A and B to tl.float16 (or bf16) before tl.dot while keeping the fp32 accumulator — TF32 on Ada is ~half the throughput of fp16 tensor cores; given 5e-2 tolerance, this is safe and roughly doubles GEMM throughput. Alternatively, store weight_t as fp16 once in __init__ and cast x at kernel entry.
- Remove the output mask (M=16384, N=4096 are exact multiples of all tile sizes in the configs) and drop the second redundant offs_m_out/offs_n_out recomputation; minor but removes a predicate from the store.
large_guidance:
- Rewrite using a split-K or stream-K persistent GEMM strategy: with M=N=16384×4096 and K=4096, a persistent kernel with one program per SM iterating over output tiles eliminates launch/tile-scheduling overhead and improves L2 reuse beyond the current GROUP_M swizzle.
- Switch the compute dtype to fp16/bf16 tensor cores (accumulate in fp32). Pre-pack weight_t as fp16 in __init__ and have the kernel cast x tiles to fp16 on load. On RTX 4090 this roughly doubles tensor-core throughput vs. TF32 and is within the 5e-2 tolerance.
- Consider a Triton "Hopper-style" warp-specialized layout or at minimum tl.load with cache modifiers (.ca for A reused across N tiles, .cg for B) and a transposed B layout `[N, K]` row-major so the inner-K load is fully contiguous per warp.
